pr_title: Fix dropouts in history_stats graphs on restart
pr_body: ## Proposed change Historically history stats has set a state of unknown at startup. This made sense when history selects were much much slower (see #16932). We can now avoid the data discontinuity by refreshing before adding the entity, and trying again later if the template can't render or the there is a problem getting the data to avoid the discontinuity in the graphs. I'm not sure if this should be considered a breaking change or not so I didn't mark it for a patch release as I'd like it to go though the next beta for feedback. Fixes #73108 ## Type of change - [ ] Dependency upgrade - [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New integration (thank you!) - [ ] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break) - [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests ## Additional information - This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes # - This PR is related to issue: - Link to documentation pull request: ## Checklist - [x] The code change is tested and works locally. - [ ] Local tests pass. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass** - [ ] There is no commented out code in this PR. - [ ] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist] - [ ] The code has been formatted using Black (`black --fast homeassistant tests`) - [x] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works. If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed: - [ ] Documentation added/updated for [www.home-assistant.io][docs-repository] If the code communicates with devices, web services, or third-party tools: - [ ] The [manifest file][manifest-docs] has all fields filled out correctly. Updated and included derived files by running: `python3 -m script.hassfest`. - [ ] New or updated dependencies have been added to `requirements_all.txt`. Updated by running `python3 -m script.gen_requirements_all`. - [ ] For the updated dependencies - a link to the changelog, or at minimum a diff between library versions is added to the PR description. - [ ] Untested files have been added to `.coveragerc`. I experienced similar "spikes", but already in May, yes, with core 2022.5.x. Though this bug wasn't present in April (in my case). So _**maybe**_ the below is _**false positive**_:
- I've checked the database, and there is also an "unavailable" value for the sensor, so in my case, in May and June, spike is caused directly by an unavailable sensor data.
- But there were no other sign, that the real sensor got unavailable, all other technical values these Sonoff/Tasmota-s reporting through MQTT has no signs of any outage. And in my experience in the past 2 years, if I have any WiFi outage, that ALWAYS last for minutes, NEVER only a single value.
- And it occurred only a few times a day. Maybe only those values experienced the "outage" that were inserted into DB for plain sensory data recording AND were read for calculating statistical values _**at the same time**_.

TLDR: _**maybe**_ the sqlalchemy thread safety bug can cause bad data ("unavailable") to be stored in DB for the real sensor, that can cause these spikes in calculated values, and this bug was present before core 2022.6.x. I repeat, maybe!
